note: Facts the model clause and the PDF's feasibility section quote, each with its public source, tag and read date. [V] = primary source read; [S] = secondary source only. Every string in `checks` is copied verbatim from the author's research notes; pipeline/tests/test_clause.py asserts that wherever those notes are present (they are not published). pipeline/clause.py renders the rows; nothing here is a number of ours.

precedents.instrument: Sustainability-linked revolver, term loan and notes
precedents.moneyTerm: Effective interest rate moves ±0.05 % a year with the number of targets met; one target is Scope 1+2 methane intensity −30 % by 2030 vs 2021
precedents.differs: Annual, company-wide, borrower-reported; the closest analogue to the refund side, but the next leak does not cancel it

precedents.moneyTerm: Coupon +0.10 % if one of two 2030 targets is missed, +0.20 % if both; one target is methane about 50 % below 2020; tested once, at 31 Dec 2030
precedents.differs: One company total, one test date; the coupon steps by indenture, not on an event at a source
checks: **up 0.10 % if one of two 2030 targets is missed, 0.20 % if both are missed**

precedents.moneyTerm: Pricing incentive linked to corporate KPIs, one of them "methane intensity in E&P"; target and step size not disclosed
precedents.differs: Company-wide intensity from the borrower's inventory; the money is the lender's margin, not a payment to the gas buyer
checks: The 6-K gives no target and no step size.

precedents.party: Pavilion Energy with QatarEnergy (SPA 2020) and Chevron (SPA 2021); methodology 2021
precedents.moneyTerm: Disclosure only: a Statement of GHG Emissions for every cargo, third-party verified; no money term found
precedents.differs: The first SPA-level methane term; a modelled cargo-chain estimate that nothing pays on
checks: Statement of GHG Emissions (SGE) for every cargo
**It is the first SPA-level methane term**, and it is disclosure only.

precedents.instrument: Optional model clauses under Art. 28(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1787
precedents.moneyTerm: No remedy term: no price adjustment, rebate, termination, liquidated damages, audit right, satellite or super-emitter reference
precedents.differs: Moves information down the chain and leaves the economic clause open; this clause is that economic clause
checks: There is no price adjustment, rebate, termination, LDs, audit right, satellite or super-emitter reference.

noPriceTerm.line: No public LNG contract with a methane-intensity price term was found; SPA price terms are usually confidential, so the claim is "no public precedent found", not "none exists".
checks: **An LNG contract with a methane-intensity price adjustment: none found in public.**
the right claim is "**no public precedent found**", not "none exists"

euDates.what: Art. 28: contracts concluded or renewed on or after this date are the ones the import MRV-equivalence obligation covers (older contracts: "all reasonable efforts")
checks: From 1 Jan 2027 importer must show contracts (concluded/renewed ≥ 4 Aug 2024)

euDates.what: Art. 28: the importer must show producer-level MRV equivalent to the EU's for those contracts (a one-year delay of reporting-related provisions was proposed on 14 Oct 2026, not adopted)
checks: From 1 Jan 2027 importer must show contracts
Commission proposed on **14 Oct 2026** to postpone "reporting-related provisions" by 1 year (needs EP+Council)

euDates.what: Art. 27 and Annex IX: the importer's yearly report to its national competent authority
checks: First report was due 5 May 2025, then 31 May yearly.

euDates.what: Recommendation (EU) 2026/1835 asks Member States not to fine importers for breaches in 2027–29, except fraud
checks: Rec. 2026/1835 asks Member States not to fine importers for 2027–29 breaches except fraud

euDates.what: Art. 29: contracts concluded or renewed after this date must stay below Commission-set maximum methane-intensity values
checks: from 5 Aug 2030 contracts concluded/renewed after that date must be *below* Commission-set maximum values

renewalExample.what: BOTAS–Bulgargaz: a long-term supply deal from 2023, frozen and put into renegotiation by protocol; a renewal moves a contract into the full Art. 28 obligation (public news; the pilot's parties stay [SIM])
checks: any **renewal** (e.g. the 2026 Bulgargaz renegotiation) flips them into full Art. 28 equivalence
